text:
mari: quick brain-dump — we need a concrete proposal for how routing policies by customer tier + quotas should behave when capacity is constrained. current ask from product: free/pro/enterprise, plus per-region constraints, and model-variant fallbacks. suggestions? :thinking:

jamal: +1 we should decide whether exceeding quota should 1) hard-block, 2) soft-degrade (downgrade model variant), or 3) best-effort with logging + billing spike. my vote: soft-degrade for free/pro, hard-block for enterprise (unless override).

sophie: telemetry must capture both the decision and outcome. e.g. `routing_decision:{tier,region,requested_model,served_model,reason}` and latency/cost delta. dashboard needs a per-tier waterfall so PMs can see how often downgrades happen.

kevin: thinking about API shape — two bits: control-plane policy and runtime signals. control-plane: JSON policy that maps tiers -> region preferences -> variant fallbacks. runtime: small header in request to opt-out of downgrades. example policy snippet: ```json
{
  "tiers": {
    "free": {"priority": ["small-quant","cpu-optim"], "quota_action": "downgrade"},
    "pro": {"priority": ["base","small-quant"], "quota_action": "downgrade"},
    "enterprise": {"priority": ["base","high-accuracy"], "quota_action": "block"}
  }
}
```

luis: region weighting matters — prefer local region unless unavailable, then cross-region fallback but mark for telemetry. also for enterprise we should allow a customer flag to permit cross-region fallback for availability.

mari: UX questions — Console needs a simple toggle for each tier: "Allow downgrades when capacity constrained" + an advanced editor to list variant order. product wants defaults that are conservative. can we autosuggest defaults based on historical latency/cost per-model?

kevin: autosuggest is doable — Optimize already has model cost profiles. runtime can sample a small % to validate fallback quality before applying broadly. need rollout UX: canary the fallback policy to 5% of requests for a tier, observe quality regressions.

sophie: dashboard panels: 1) downgrade rate per tier, 2) avg quality metric pre/post downgrade (from evals), 3) cost delta, 4) latency changes. also we should surface customer-visible errors when blocked (standardized error code like `quota.blocked.model_unavailable`).

jamal: implementation risk: when KV cache mismatch happens between model variants, downgrades could regress coherency for chat sessions. runtime needs to clear session cache or detect incompatible cache and fall back to stateless degrade. we should add `compatibility` metadata to variants.

ops-bot: alert rule suggestion: fire if downgrade rate for a tier > 2% sustained for 10m AND quality drop > 5% :rotating_light:.

mari: timeline: prototype policy editor + control-plane rules for tiers by EOW next week, runtime enforcement + telemetry in two sprints. can we scope console to toggle + a read-only inferred list initially?

kevin: API detail: request header `x-redwood-prefer-no-downgrade: true` — if set, runtime should attempt only requested model then error; respects enterprise overrides. also include `x-redwood-tier` in logs for easier joins.

luis: question on quotas: do we count quota on requested model or served model? counting requested makes enterprise safe but can be gamed. counting served penalizes downgrade. propose counting requested for billing/quota, but log both for fairness.

mari: agreed count requested for quota, but include `served_model` in billing/cost-calcs so product can evaluate.

deploy-bot: deployed `policy-service:v2` to staging with the new tier schema (no runtime changes yet).

sophie: I'll mock dashboard visuals and sample telemetry events today and attach a brief spec. can we meet 11am PT to align on fallbacks?

jamal: 11am works. I'll bring the runtime compatibility checklist. :thumbsup:
